questions.prompt: One cell divides 5 times, and every new cell divides each time. How many cells are there?
A bacterium divides every 20 minutes. Starting with one, how many are there after 2 hours?
How does a cut on your knee heal?
options: Old cells stretch to fill the gap
Cells near the cut divide to make new cells

questions.explain: Many unicellular organisms reproduce by dividing into two.

questions.prompt: Why is it safer to put leftover cooked rice in the fridge rather than leaving it out overnight?
options: The fridge makes it taste better
Cold slows down how fast bacteria divide, so far fewer build up
Bacteria die instantly in the fridge
questions.explain: At room temperature bacteria can double every 20–30 minutes.

questions.prompt: About how many doublings would it take to go from 1 cell to more than 1000 cells?
Street-food stalls often keep food out for hours in hot weather. Using what you know about how bacteria multiply, suggest three rules a vendor could follow to keep food safe.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Cook food fresh in small batches and sell it quickly, so bacteria have little time to multiply. 2) Keep cooked food either very hot or cold (in an ice box), because bacteria divide fastest at warm temperatures. 3) Cover food and use clean water and utensils, to reduce the number of bacteria that get in to start with. Also wash hands and throw away leftovers at the end of the day.
questions.explain: Criterion D: apply science to public health.
